issues.description: Fix payload `text: '0deg'` contradicts the diff `range: [31, 32]` for the `10` -> `10deg` case
issues.detail: In the new reject test `oklch(from red l c 10) -> oklch(from red l c 10deg)`, the recorded fix is `range: [31, 32], text: '0deg'`. Range [31,32] covers a single character (the `0` of `10`), and replacing it with `0deg` yields `1` + `0deg` = `10deg`, which technically lands. But it is the wrong shape: the actual edit is appending `deg` after `10`, which is `range: [33, 33], text: 'deg'`. The test now codifies a fixer that mutates the digit rather than appending the unit. Either the underlying fixer really does this (in which case it's bad-taste code that should be fixed) or the test is asserting an incidentally-equivalent-but-misleading edit. Same shape repeats in the `hsl(from red 10 s l)` case. Pin down which it is before landing.

`return args[0 + offset];` reads worse than `return args[offset];`. The `0 +` adds nothing and the reader has to confirm it adds nothing. Match the surrounding voice; write `args[offset]` and `args[2 + offset]` only because the 2 there means something.

issues.description: `isRelativeColor` is computed but only used to derive `offset`
issues.detail: Two-line setup for a single one-shot derivation. Collapse to `const offset = args[0]?.value.toLowerCase() === 'from' ? 2 : 0;` with a comment. Not load-bearing, but the named boolean is dead weight given it's never referenced again.

issues.description: Relative color base can itself be a color function; offset of 2 is not always correct
issues.detail: The accept test `oklch(from hsl(270deg 60% 50%) l c h)` correctly survives because `args` filters to `word|function` and the inner `hsl(...)` is a single function arg, so `args` is `[from, hsl(...), l, c, h]` and `offset = 2` lands on `l`. Good. But this depends on `node.nodes` having the inner function as a single sibling and not getting split. Worth a defensive note or test asserting the args array shape, because if a future postcss-value-parser change splits these differently, this silently regresses. Not a blocker, but the assumption deserves a comment.

issues.description: No test for `color()` / `color(from ...)` if rule applies, and no negative test for non-relative `from` keyword positioning edge
issues.detail: Coverage is good for `hsl`, `lch`, `oklch`. If `hue-degree-notation` is supposed to ignore the keyword `from` appearing in odd positions (e.g. as a custom property fallback), there's no test pinning that. Add at least one test where `from` appears but is not at `args[0]`, to lock the heuristic.

review.summary: Small patch, one real problem to solve, scoped to one function. Good taste in shape: detect relative-color syntax once, offset the index, reuse the existing branches. That's the right diff. The concerns are: (1) the fix-range/text payloads in two new reject tests look off — `range: [31, 32], text: '0deg'` for an append-`deg` edit is at best misleading and at worst encoding a sloppy fixer; verify against the actual fixer behavior. (2) Cosmetic noise: `0 + offset` and a one-use `isRelativeColor` boolean. NEEDS-WORK on the test payload question; the rest is style. Once the fix-range mystery is resolved, this lands.
